text: Council ruling (pick US): NU. NU gets the $100 because its 14.44% three-month momentum, 50.2% latest-quarter revenue growth, and 66.3% earnings growth give it the clearest chance of beating the S&P 500 through November 30. Its forward price-to-earnings ratio of 14.17 and price-to-earnings-growth ratio of 0.74 are attractive, while Financials gained 2.17% over five days. The November 12 earnings event could help or hurt sharply, so this remains a low-confidence, short-horizon paper trade where noise can overwhelm the thesis. I assume a US zero-commission fractional-share account: stated round-trip charges are approximately zero on $100, although spreads remain a hidden cost and any short-term gain is taxed according to the client's residency, federal bracket, and state. The 10x goal is separate: even steady 12% annual compounding would require 20.3 years, so this call only seeks to beat the index over 35 trading days.

speaker: Gemini
text: Regarding your $100 NVDA trade: at current prices, a $100 investment buys you a fractional slice of the company, but don't expect a 10x return in a year; that would require an impossible leap in valuation. For the auto and battery sector, keep an eye on Tata Motors and Exide Industries, but remember that these are cyclical, capital-intensive plays that rarely deliver the exponential growth needed for your 10x goal. NU remains our spotlight; its 50.2% revenue growth is impressive, but with a 1.39 beta, it will swing violently with the broader market. Stay disciplined with your costs—they eat your gains faster than you think.

text: On fundamentals NU still screens cheap for its growth: forward P/E of 14.17 with a PEG of 0.74 against 50.2% revenue growth is rare, and quarterly net income has climbed from $637M to $1.06B in five quarters.
